plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets two congruent parallelograms side by side, outlined in dark blue with both diagonals drawn as thin lines, to place vector addition next to vector subtraction. In the left parallelogram the bottom edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing right and is labeled u; the slanted right-hand edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing up and to the right and is labeled v; and the diagonal running from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner ends in an orange arrowhead and is labeled u + v. The right parallelogram repeats the same outline, but its top edge is the one labeled u with an orange arrowhead pointing right, its slanted right-hand edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing down and to the right and is labeled -v, its bottom edge is also labeled u, and the diagonal that descends from the upper-left corner toward the lower-right corner is labeled u - v. Drawing both results inside the same shape shows that the sum and the difference are simply the two diagonals of one parallelogram. The pairing makes the point that u - v is built by reversing v and joining it head to tail with u.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The only change from u + v to u - v is that v is reversed to -v, which makes the resultant the other completed diagonal.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Render the default state as the fully completed two-panel textbook figure, not as a hidden or partially constructed scene. Keep both panels visible in every interaction state; emphasis should use a subtle glow, slightly stronger color, or temporary path cue only, never fading out the inactive panel or hiding labels. Use slender orange arrows with small arrowheads and moderate stroke weight so they match textbook styling rather than thick vector graphics. Draw construction parallelogram outlines in dark blue, with orange used for the active component and resultant arrows. In the addition panel, place u along the bottom edge pointing right, v on the right slanted edge pointing up-right, and u + v on the rising diagonal. In the subtraction panel, place u along the top edge pointing right, -v on the right slanted edge pointing down-right, and u - v on the descending diagonal. Labels should be visible in their final positions from the start. For interaction state and click handling, use only the ASCII operation keys 'addition' and 'subtraction'; display text may show mathematical minus signs, but handler logic should not mix '-' and '−'.

plan.authoredInteractions:

- Button for construction steps: the learner steps through drawing u, placing v or -v head-to-tail, completing the parallelogram, and revealing the diagonal, making the result vector depend on the order of geometric construction.

authoredContext:
Vector subtraction is similar to vector addition. To find u − v, view it as u + (−v). Adding −v is reversing direction of v and adding it to the end of u. The new vector begins at the start of u and stops at the end point of −v. See the figure for a visual that compares vector addition and vector subtraction using parallelograms.

Showing vector addition and subtraction with parallelograms. For addition, the base is u, the side is v, the diagonal connecting the start of the base to the end of the side is u+v. For subtraction, thetop is u, the side is -v, and the diagonal connecting the start of the top to the end of the side is u-v.

interactions.label: Operation
interactions.teaches: Switching from addition to subtraction reverses v into -v and changes which diagonal represents the resultant vector

interactions.label: Construction steps
interactions.teaches: The resultant vector is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the placed second vector, after the component vectors have been arranged head to tail
Each diagonal of the parallelogram corresponds to a different pair of directed side vectors: one diagonal represents u + v, while the other represents u - v

demo_steps.title: Start with u
demo_steps.narration: Begin with the horizontal vector u. In addition mode it is drawn along the bottom edge, pointing to the right.

demo_steps.title: Place v head to tail
demo_steps.narration: Now place v so its tail starts at the head of u. The slanted side points up and to the right, forming the second side of the path.

demo_steps.title: Reveal the sum diagonal
demo_steps.narration: Completing the parallelogram shows that u + v is the diagonal from the starting point of u to the final head of v.

demo_steps.title: Reverse v for subtraction
demo_steps.narration: Switch to subtraction: v reverses direction and becomes -v. The construction is now u + (-v), not a new kind of vector operation.

demo_steps.title: Reveal the difference diagonal
demo_steps.narration: The resultant u - v is the other diagonal of the same parallelogram, running from the tail of u to the head of -v. Click either diagonal to highlight its component vectors.

plan.keyInsight: Subtraction of vectors is addition of the opposite vector, so u - v is built by reversing v and drawing the diagonal to the new endpoint.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean white background with a single dark blue parallelogram centered in the scene, or show the addition and subtraction versions as toggle states of the same congruent shape. The outline should be dark blue and fairly thick; construction diagonals should be thinner blue unless active. Use orange for active vector arrows and arrowheads. In addition mode, emphasize bottom u, right-side v, and the rising diagonal labeled u + v. In subtraction mode, emphasize top u, right-side -v directed downward, the bottom parallel u as a reference, and the descending diagonal labeled u - v. Labels should be black italic math-style text placed close to their corresponding sides or diagonals.

discrepancies: The source shows two parallelogram panels side by side for addition and subtraction, while the default generated view shows only one enlarged addition construction panel.
The default state is only the first construction step: the active v arrow and the orange resultant u + v diagonal arrow from the source's left panel are missing or only shown faintly.
The subtraction diagram with top u, right-side −v, and the u − v diagonal is not visible in the default static view.
The orange u arrowhead is much larger and heavier than in the source, making the proportions of the vector arrows noticeably inaccurate.
Important labels from the source, especially −v and u − v, are absent by default, and the visible v and u + v labels are faded rather than matching the black source labels.
Clicking the difference diagonal uses a Unicode minus in the operation string, so it does not reliably switch/render the subtraction state despite the popup claiming it has.
evaluation.notes: The parallelogram construction is recognizable and has useful step controls, but the default view is not a faithful replacement for the two-panel source figure and omits most final-vector content.

Fix the subtraction click handler by using a consistent operation string or boolean state instead of mixing ASCII '-' and Unicode '−'.
